summary: Kamala Tiyavanich specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, and held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.
Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held academic posts at Brown University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

Kamil Zvelebil (1927–2009) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Charles University circa 1946–1952 and held positions at the Oriental Institute, ASCR (circa 1952–1968), and Utrecht University (1980–1990).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indology and religious studies scholar who taught Hisayoshi Miyamoto and Shujun Motegi. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University and served as an advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and earned her PhD from the University of Virginia (circa 2001–2009) under David Germano and Paul Groner, later holding a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.

Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Ceylon (circa 1965–1968) under Sirima Kiribamune, also studied under Sukumar Sengupta, and was a Pali lecturer at Calcutta.
Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a teaching post at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and later served as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yun-hua Jan (attested 1976), later holding an academic post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
Kang-yuan Sung works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Calgary (attested 1999) under supervisor A. W. Barber, also studying under Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Paris and under Takamatsu Yoshie, and later held a post at the Tokyo National Museum.

Kanoko Tanaka specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Muni Tulsi and held an appointment as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962). He held a post as lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University, and served as Academic Director at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts circa 1987–2000.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. In 1968, he taught Sanskrit and Indian philosophy and religion at Cambridge and Durham, later serving as Honorary Professorial Research Associate at SOAS (circa 1993–2019).

Karen C. Lang specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as professor at the University of Virginia.

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who taught Johan Elverskog. She completed her studies at Smith College (circa 1960–1964), Union Theological Seminary (circa 1964–1966), and Temple University (circa 1970–1976).

Karen Nelson Villanueva works in philosophy and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013) and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero, who taught Sally McAra, held academic appointments at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her PhD and served as a senior teaching fellow at SOAS, later becoming a lecturer in Asian Religions and Ethics at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020).

Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as assistant professor and director of the Buddhist studies MA program at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
